packages.label: שִׂמְחָה וְרִקּוּדִין וְתִקּוּן הַחוֹלֶה
packages.label_en: Joy, Dancing, and the Healing of Illness
packages.reason: All four nodes in this package share the same essential reality: that joy and dancing ARE healing — they are not the instrument of healing but healing itself. The Rebbe states explicitly (1) 'הַשִּׂמְחָה הִיא בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַחוֹלֶה' (simcha IS tikkun hacholeh) and (2) 'וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה נִקְרָאִין הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהָרִקּוּדִין חוֹלָה' (simcha and dancing ARE CALLED choleh). The word 'choleh' is deliberately polysemous: it means both 'sick person' and 'circle dance' (mahol / rosh holeh). Joy is the healing of illness (tikkun hacholeh); dancing is itself the circle (choleh); and all of these are facets of one essential domain: simcha as the curative reality. The two raw components {שמחה והרקודין, חולה} and {שמחה, תקון החולה} are merged because 'שמחה' and 'שמחה והרקודין' share the same essential nature (dancing is the embodied expression of simcha, not its effect), and 'חולה' and 'תקון החולה' are the same domain — the pivot word 'choleh' that means both sickness and dance. The Rebbe's wordplay makes these four expressions of one unified truth.

merge_notes.reason: Raw component A was merged into the main package rather than kept separate. 'שמחה והרקודין' is not a distinct domain from 'שמחה' — dancing is the embodied form of simcha, sharing the same essential nature (bechina), not a causal product of it. Likewise 'חולה' (the sick person / circle dance) belongs to the same domain as 'תקון החולה' (healing of illness) because the Rebbe's point is precisely that these are the same word — choleh = sick / choleh = circle dance. The merge is grounded in shared nature, not cause-and-effect.
